subject: Post-demo: embedding adoption readiness & migration checklist
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@storify.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Park <jordan.park@storify.ai>
Date: Tue, 09 Jan 2028 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Embeddings export + questions from demo

Connor / Marissa — thanks again for the walkthrough today. A few things we want to capture formally from the call so our infra and search teams can triage: 

1) Current export: attached is a sample of our current embeddings export (storify_embeddings_export_v3.csv). It’s 1536-d (from our current vendor) and includes a mix of sentence and short-paragraph records.

2) Dimensionality concerns: we heard you recommending 768/1024 in the demo. We need guidance on concrete tradeoffs (latency/cost/quality) if we (a) down-project from 1536→1024 or 1536→768 vs (b) replace with native 1024 model embeddings.

3) Batching/throughput: our traffic for index builds is bursty (daily bulk re-index + steady small writes). We need recommended batch sizes and guidance on dual-write vs cutover for steady-state to keep searches live during migration.

4) Normalization & scoring: do you recommend L2-normalized vectors on our side? Anything special for reranker integration (we use a lightweight reranker service before final scoring)?

5) Auth & routing: our security team needs a short checklist for auth (API keys vs short-lived tokens) and how routing to a fallback variant would work if dedicated capacity is saturated.

6) SLA/cost estimate: rough bandwidth/price delta vs our current provider for 100M monthly embedding tokens (ballpark answer ok).

Can you reply with a concise next-steps list and any artifacts (SDK snippet, migration checklist) we can hand to infra? We’d like to schedule a 45-min deep dive with Karthik and your infra lead early next week.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Search — Storify

Attachment: storify_embeddings_export_v3.csv (CSV, 9.8 MB)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@storify.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jan 2028 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Embeddings export + questions from demo

Alex — great questions, summing up and adding recommended next steps so your infra/search teams have a checklist. Per our call notes below.

Quick answers up front:
- Dimensionality: we generally recommend re-embedding to 1024 if you can tolerate re-embedding cost; down-projecting 1536→1024 (via PCA) usually preserves ~98% of nearest-neighbor quality on paragraph-level content and gives ~15–25% lower token cost depending on model. 768 is cheaper but starts trading off on semantic nuance in longer queries.
- Normalization: yes — L2 normalization on your side is simplest and compatible with Redwood’s cosine/L2-backed indexes and rerankers.
- Batching: for export/import use batches of 5k–20k items for bulk jobs (tune by payload size); for runtime writes, use micro-batches (64–256) with concurrent workers. We can provide an autoscaling pattern for your side.
- Migration strategy: 1) dual-write (write to old provider + Redwood), 2) shadow-querying (periodic scoring comparison), 3) progressive cutover (traffic % canary) — we’ll provide a checklist.
- Auth/routing: we support scoped API keys and short-lived JWTs via OIDC (recommended for service accounts). Routing policies can be configured by customer tier, region, or latency SLO; automatic fallback to a smaller/quantized variant is supported.

Proposed next steps (what we can deliver before the deep dive):
A) Redwood: SDK snippet for embeddings upsert + query (Python + Node), auth example (short-lived token), a migration playbook PDF, and a sample cost estimate for 100M tokens/month.
B) Storify: provide a representative export (you already attached)—we'll run a sample re-embed and perf test on our side.
C) Schedule: 45-min deep dive with Karthik + infra (please propose Tue/Wed next week).

I attached our high-level playbook and a short runbook for dual-write/cutover. If helpful I can also run a short POC (free) against a 10k subset to show latency/cost deltas.

—Connor

- Reranker latency: our current reranker adds ~12–18 ms per candidate. If we change embedding dims, what end-to-end delta should we expect for a 10-candidate rerank stage? Any recommendations to keep P95 low?
- Quantization: we currently use 8-bit PQ in the vector DB. How does Redwood handle quantized indexes and does that affect similarity behavior if we down-project first?
- Vendor parity: our procurement team asked if we can do a direct compare (A/B) versus our current provider (VecCloud) with identical queries and result labels. What's the simplest way to get statistically comparable logs?

Also: Wed/Tue windows work for us. Karthik — can you share the SDK snippet and a short auth example ahead of the call so our infra team can pre-review?

—Alex

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@storify.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jan 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Embeddings export + questions from demo — SDK + auth example

Alex — adding the concrete snippets and short answers below so your infra team can review before the deep dive.

1) SDK upsert (Python) — minimal example:

from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk.scope.storage:ingest")
# upsert a batch
batch = [ {"id": "doc-123", "vector": vec, "metadata": {"lang": "en"} } for vec in vectors ]
client.embeddings.upsert(index="storify-prod", vectors=batch)

2) Auth example: short-lived JWT via OIDC (recommended for service accounts). We issue tokens via your IdP (SCIM service account) and Redwood validates via JWKS. If you prefer static keys we support scoped API keys with limited index privileges.

3) Reranker latency: dimensionality change (1536→1024) typically reduces similarity compute by ~25–30% in the vector step; end-to-end rerank delta for 10 candidates is usually ~5–12 ms improvement depending on your CPU/GPU split. To keep P95 low: prefer async micro-batching + local candidate prefetching and cache hot candidates at the edge.

4) Quantization: Redwood supports PQ/OPQ + 8-bit quantization in indexes. Down-projecting before quantization is fine — we recommend re-projecting and then applying quantization on the target dim to keep similarity behavior predictable. We'll include an A/B log collection template for statistical comparison.

5) Vendor parity plan: we’ll do a shadow-compare flow: identical queries logged to both providers, aggregate MRR / recall at k, and then sample label a couple thousand queries for subjective diffs. I attached a short template for log schema and expected fields.

I can push a small repo with the SDK snippet + a migration checklist to the Drive link in Connor's note before EOD. Which slot do you prefer for the deep dive — Tue 10am or Wed 2pm PST?

—Karthik
Senior ML Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
